No authorial verification label, objection marker, explicit proof check or question mark is unambiguously identified on this page. The upper-margin crossed-stem and parallel-stroke signs are not converted into authorial doubt marks.

The only actual mathematical check in this first reading is the elementary quotient-group kernel-stability statement recorded below. No geometric lifting theorem, existence assertion, or uniqueness assertion on this incomplete page was proved. No OCR, external research, or LaTeX compilation was used.

For the opening Si issue, absence is asserted only of a separately live word outside the deletion: overlapping strokes inside the cancelled cluster could contain an older Si-like trace. The old cluster remains uncertain rather than being declared fully deciphered.

Follow-up punctuation check: a single permitted tight crop of rev. shows a separate dark terminal dot after the v, agreeing with C and H. No new uncertainty or change row is warranted at rev. The written double quotes around K-connexe, absence of H’s semicolon after the second restriction definition, and absence of H’s comma after groupoïdes are recorded as substantive punctuation differences.

Main-reader adjudication of the lower note: en supposant is the first tentative reading, with ne supposant as alternative. A negative hypothesis would make mathematical sense when broadening the allowable point, but that expectation is recorded here only; it neither proves nor establishes the written wording. The possible pas remains marked as low doubt.

check_events.statement: For a group homomorphism u:G→H and α∈Aut(G), the equality α(ker u)=ker u is equivalent to α inducing an automorphism of G/ker u, hence of im(u), by g ker u ↦ α(g) ker u.
check_events.place: Condition 3, the kernel-stability sentence; elementary algebraic part only.
check_events.outcome: Verified directly in this run: if α preserves the kernel, equality of cosets is preserved and α⁻¹ also preserves the kernel, so the induced map is an automorphism. Conversely an induced automorphism compatible with the quotient forces α and α⁻¹ to send the kernel into itself, yielding equality. This does not verify the asserted geometric existence of Θ′ or authorize changing x to x′.
